_comment: Plate spec for Scene 1. One entry per manifest shot, under 'shots'.
A shot's plate is its OWN validated v4 storyboard panel from the 9/9 PASS
set (r2:rex-assets/storyboards/v4/scene-01/). Those panels are locked,
approved artifacts, so for gating purposes the panel IS the plate. Nothing
here was drawn or generated for the gate.
Boxes are normalised [x0, y0, x1, y1] against that shot's own plate, so a
candidate frame of any resolution or aspect can be compared to it.
Everything is measured off the plate itself - the plate is the source of
truth, this file only says WHERE to look and HOW CLOSE is close enough.
A check only runs when this file gives that shot the inputs it needs:
layout_match         needs 'regions'
staging_orientation  needs 'bands'
couch_occupancy      needs regions.couch AND swatches.couch_upholstery
wardrobe             needs 'swatches' + 'wardrobe' + manifest characters
A close-up has no couch band, so it gets no couch check - rather than a
bogus one. Fewer honest checks beat many invented ones.
Regenerate a plate jpg (byte-identical to the ones committed here):
rclone copy r2:rex-assets/storyboards/v4/scene-01/scene-01-1A-start.png /tmp/
ffmpeg -i /tmp/scene-01-1A-start.png -vf scale=512:-2 -q:v 3 plate/scene-01-1A-plate.jpg
_thresholds_comment: Scene-wide defaults. A shot entry may override any of them under its own
'thresholds' key; the merged result is what that shot is scored on.
min_applied_checks is the anti-thin-plate rule. A frame on which fewer than
this many checks could actually be applied is INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS. It is
here because VIDEO-GATE.md records 02-shot-1B passing on a single colour
check (Leo's green) while the room behind him was the wrong room. One
measurement is an anecdote, not a clearance.

_comment: The original plate, unchanged. Regions, bands, swatches, wardrobe map
and thresholds are exactly what shipped in task #336 - every 1A number
in VIDEO-GATE.md's corpus table still reproduces.
1A._bands_comment: The locked staging puts the TV in the left band and Jenny's armchair in the right band; a flipped room scores better crossed than straight.

_comment: Medium on Leo, static with a slight push. No TV and no armchair in
frame, but the couch fills the lower two thirds and the left/right
asymmetry is real: warm lamp and bookshelf screen-left, cold stormy
window screen-right. Mia is at the extreme frame edge and the manifest
says so, so she stays unmeasured.
1B.framing: medium on Leo, static with slight push

_comment: Medium TRACKING shot, 15s left to right. The regions below are real -
front door and Gabe screen-left, stormy window and Jenny's chair
screen-right - but they only hold near the head of the track. See the
camera-move note in VIDEO-GATE.md; this shot's layout threshold is
deliberately not tuned down to make a moving camera pass.
1C.framing: medium tracking, camera moves left to right
1C.cannot_clear_reason: 1C can only FAIL a clip, never clear one: the 1B, 1D and 1I panels all walk straight through this gate (measured by score_corpus.py --cross-shot). Its layout, staging and wardrobe cannot separate this medium from its neighbours in the same warm dim room.

_comment: Two-shot, static with occasional reframes. Both parents are in black,
so their swatches disqualify themselves the same way they do on 1A -
but Mia's magenta, Leo's green and Jenny's grey-blue are all present at
background scale in this plate, and because the plate IS this framing
that scale is the right reference. Hence background_characters:
measure.
Close-up insert on Jenny, static, 5s. Shallow depth of field: the
background is deliberately blurred, so there is no couch band worth
measuring and no second costume. Jenny fills the middle third.
1E.cannot_clear_reason: 1E can only FAIL a clip, never clear one: the 1D panel passes this gate (measured by score_corpus.py --cross-shot). Jenny's grey-olive hoodie is unmeasurable in this light, so layout is doing all the work and it cannot tell this close-up from the two-shot.

_comment: Close-up insert on the TV, static, 4s. The manifest lists no characters
at all, so wardrobe is n/a by definition and this shot is carried by
geometry alone. The screen region is the least stable thing in the
scene - the cartoon on it is meant to move and to flare with static -
so the bezel, the window and the armchair do most of the work.
OTS from behind the kids, static, 30s. Mia's silhouette screen-left,
Leo's screen-right, the TV between them and the parents in the warm
middle distance. The manifest marks all four characters OTS or
background, but this plate is that framing, so their scale here is the
correct reference - background_characters: measure. Mia's magenta back
and Leo's green pyjama sleeve are both large and unambiguous.
1G.framing: OTS from behind the kids, static
1G.cannot_clear_reason: 1G can only FAIL a clip, never clear one: the 1A wide passes this gate (measured by score_corpus.py --cross-shot). Every costume colour here is too dark to measure, so layout is alone and an OTS of this room reads much like a wide of it.

_comment: Close-up on Mia, slow push, 20s. Only one character, and her magenta
top is the one costume colour in Scene 1 that is unambiguous. The
parents are out-of-focus silhouettes at both edges; the stormy window
screen-right against the warm lamp screen-left is the framing's real
left/right signature.
background_characters: measure because the manifest note for Mia here
is 'looking up at off-screen parents' - the substring 'off-screen'
describes where she is LOOKING, not where she is. She fills the frame.
Close-up to two-shot, static then a 77s pull. Both costumes are black
formalwear, so wardrobe disqualifies itself here exactly as it does on
1A - this shot is carried by geometry. The hallway is strongly
asymmetric (coat rack and flowers screen-left, stormy window
screen-right), which is what makes the mirror test worth running.
1I.framing: close-up to two-shot, static then pull
1I.cannot_clear_reason: 1I can only FAIL a clip, never clear one: the 1C panel passes this gate (measured by score_corpus.py --cross-shot, layout 0.764 against a 0.55 threshold). Both costumes are black formalwear and both shots are the same hallway, so nothing here separates them.
